summary: Client transport backpressure + small connection pool => serialized request queueing and timeouts for Novacore
description: Issue summary: Customer Novacore reported large spike in end-to-end inference latency and several request timeouts starting 2026-03-10 09:15 UTC. Impact: interactive product queries returned 10-30s responses or 504 after retries, affecting ~1200 user-facing requests/minute for their dedicated cluster. Environment: dedicated pool in us-west-2, SDK client v1.8.3 used by Novacore backend (Node.js), concurrency target ~40 QPS. Observed failure pattern: service-side metrics showed steady backend processing times (~150ms/token) while customer-facing p95/p99 latency was high and many requests were queued in the customer SDK process.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Novacore-like Node SDK 1.8.3 with default maxConnections=6 and default retry/backoff config.
2) Generate sustained burst of concurrent requests (~40 concurrent requests) to a pinned model on a dedicated pool.
3) Observe client-side request queue depth growing and per-request latency increasing; after retries, some calls fail with 504 or timeout.
4) Reproduce locally by configuring a small connection pool with high concurrency and synthetic load generator.
observed_behavior: Client-side queueing in SDK serialized requests due to connection pool exhaustion and aggressive retry logic. Backend served requests fine; apparent slowness is client-side queuing and backoff windows that compounded under burst load.
expected_behavior: SDK should maintain enough concurrent connections to keep requests parallel up to configured client concurrency and apply exponential backoff with jitter so that retries don't serialize live traffic.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: backend regression or serving runtime CPU pressure. Confirmed: serving runtime latency and GPU metrics looked healthy; per-token timing unchanged. Correlated customer-side telemetry showed connection pool saturation and long queue wait times inside SDK. Packet capture and metrics from Novacore revealed client kept only 6 concurrent HTTP/1.1 connections to the API; with Node event loop and serialized retries, requests were effectively sequentialized once a few requests hit long backoffs. Reproduced in lab by running SDK v1.8.3 with maxConnections=6 and 40 parallel workers: p99 client-side latency matched customer reports. Patch path: SDK change to increase default maxConnections to 50 for high-concurrency use, add adaptive pool sizing, and change retry implementation to avoid global serialization (PR linked). Temporary mitigation for customer: increase SDK maxConnections to 40 and enable connection keepalive and HTTP/2 multiplexing; adjust retry policy to max 2 retries with jitter.
resolution_notes: Worked with Novacore to apply temporary client-side config: set maxConnections=40, enable http2=true, and upgrade SDK to 1.8.5 (contains non-blocking retry fix). Observed p95 drop from ~12s to ~280ms within two minutes of change. We merged SDK fix PR and published 1.8.5. Additionally, added docs section and runbook steps for connection pool sizing in the SDK README. Follow-up: engineering to monitor rollout and consider server-side rate shaping for tenants with bursty traffic (ticket INT-341 to track internal work).
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage done; backend metrics ok, flagged client-side queueing. Notified SRE and assigned Marco.
Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced locally with Novacore's config; connection pool size too small for concurrency. Preparing SDK recommendation and PR.
Novacore (Customer): Applied recommended settings and saw immediate improvement. Requested longer-term SDK fix and docs.
Elena Gomez (SDK): Merged PR #1298 that adds adaptive pool sizing and non-blocking retry; released 1.8.5. Added release notes and migration instructions.
